# Lab 27.1: BigQuery REST API & Jobs

## What We Are Going to Do
Insert a query job with the REST API, poll it until it finishes, and read the results, to understand what every tool does under the hood.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Insert a query job.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
cat &gt; job.json &lt;&lt;'EOF'
{"configuration": {"query": {
  "query": "SELECT corpus, SUM(word_count) AS words FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare` GROUP BY corpus ORDER BY words DESC LIMIT 5",
  "useLegacySql": false}},
 "jobReference": {"location": "US"}}
EOF
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://bigquery.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/jobs" -d @job.json &gt; job_resp.json
JOB_ID=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('job_resp.json'))['jobReference']['jobId'])")
echo $JOB_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Poll the job state.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://bigquery.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/jobs/$JOB_ID?location=US" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;j=json.load(sys.stdin);print(j['status']['state'], j['statistics'].get('totalBytesProcessed'))"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   States go `PENDING → RUNNING → DONE`. A `DONE` job may still have an `errorResult`.

3. **[CLI] Read the results.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://bigquery.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/queries/$JOB_ID?location=US" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;r=json.load(sys.stdin);[print([c['v'] for c in row['f']]) for row in r.get('rows',[])]"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[CLI] The shortcut: jobs.query.** Short queries can run and return in one call:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://bigquery.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/queries" \
  -d '{"query": "SELECT 1 + 1 AS two", "useLegacySql": false, "location": "US"}'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Find the API job.** It appears in **Personal history** like any other job.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| `jobs.insert` | Starts any job type |
| `jobs.get` | Poll state and statistics |
| `getQueryResults` | Read rows |
| `jobs.query` | One call for short queries |
